121736.sol: The members of phaeophyceae or brown algae are found primarily in marine habitats. They show great variation in size and form. They range from simple branched, filamentous forms (Ectocarpus) to profusely branched forms as represented by kelps, which may reach a height of 100 meters. They possess chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids and xanthophylls. They vary in color from olive green to various shades of brown depending upon the amount of the xanthophyll pigment, fucoxanthin present in them. Food is stored as complex car

121831.subject: Botany
121831.text: What type of plants are included in gymnosperms?
options: Medium-sized trees, tall trees, and shrubs
121831.sol: The gymnosperms (gymnos : naked, sperma : seeds) are plants in which the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed, both before and after fertilization. The seeds that develop post-fertilisation, are not covered, i.e., are naked. Gymnosperms include medium-sized trees or tall trees and shrubs (Figure 3.4). One of the gymnosperms, the giant redwood tree Sequoia is one of the tallest tree species. The roots are generally tap roots. Roots in some genera have fungal association in the form of mycorrh

Assertion: The Gymnosperms are plants in which the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed, both before and after fertilization. Reason: The seeds that develop post fertilization, are covered by walls.

121949.sol: The Gymnosperms are plants in which the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed, both befor and after fertilization. The seeds that develop post fertilization, are not covered i.e. naked.

122096.subject: Botany
122096.text: Assertion : Petroplants produce large amount of latex. Reason: The latex contains long chain hydrocarbons.

If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.

Such plants having large amount of latex with long chain hydrocarbons are called petroplants. Cultivation of petroplants is also a part of energy-cropping. They are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic and coelomate animals.Body is covered by a calcareous shell and is unsegmented with a distinct head,muscular foot and visceral hump in Molluscs. 123077.subject: Botany
123077.text: The technical term used for the androecium in a flower of China rose (Hibiscus rosa sinensis) is
123077.sol: In monadelphous condition, all filaments become fused and form a group, while anther remain free, e g , China rose Achyranthes, etc. In diadelphous, two separate bundles of united filaments are formed, eg, pea. In polyadelphous, more than two separate bundles of filaments are formed, eg, Ricinus.

123471.subject: Botany
123471.text: Select the correct pair amongst the following
options: Spring wood – light colour, high density
Spring wood – dark colour, low density
Autumn wood – light colour, high density
Autumn wood – dark colour, high density
123471.sol: The yearly growth of secondary xylem is distinct in the area which experiences two seasons, one favourable (spring or rainy season) and the other unfavourable (autumn, winter and dry summer). The wood formed in a single year consists of two types of wood, spring wood and autumn wood. The spring or early wood is much wider than the autumn or late wood. It is lighter in colour and of lower density. Spring wood consists of larger and wider xylem elements. The autumn or late wood is dark coloured and of higher density.

124010.subject: Botany
124010.text: What is the main function of the cell wall in plants and fungi?
options: To give shape to the cell
To protect the cell from infection
To provide a barrier to undesirable macromolecules
124010.sol: As you may recall, a non-living rigid structure called the cell wall forms an outer covering for the plasma membrane of fungi and plants. Cell wall not only gives shape to the cell and protects the cell from mechanical damage and infection, it also helps in cell-to-cell interaction and provides barrier to undesirable macromolecules. Algae have cell wall, made of cellulose, galactans, mannans and minerals like calcium carbonate, while in other plants it consists of cellulose, hemicellulose, pectins and proteins.

124718.subject: Botany
124718.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): The gaseous plant growth regulator that promotes female flowers in cucumbers also helps plants to increase their absorption surface. Reason (R): This hormone promotes root growth and root hair formation. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
124718.sol: The gaseous plant growth regulator being referred to is ethylene, which is known to promote female flowers in cucumbers, thereby increasing the yield. Assertion (A) is true because ethylene helps plants to increase their absorption surface. Reason (R) is true because ethylene achieves this by promoting root growth and root hair formation. The formation of root hairs directly increases the surface area available for absorption of water and minerals. Thus, both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) correctly explains how the

125726.subject: Botany
125726.text: Assertion : Stomata remain open during day. Reason : Stomata help in exchange of gases.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explantion of Assertion
If both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
If Assertion is true but Reason is false
If Assertion is false but Reason is true.
125726.sol: The opening and closing of stomata is a function of turgor changes in guard cells. In light malic acid is produced in guard cells which dissociates into hydrogen and malate ions, resulting in intake of K ⁺ ions through H ⁺- K ⁺ ion exchange. There is increase in concentration of K ⁺ and malate ions in guard cells, endosmosis of water into guard cells occurs resulting in increased turgor pressure which results in stomatal opening. Stomata are chiefly concerned with gaseous exchange during photosynthesis and respirat

126409.subject: Botany
126409.text: The technique of obtaining large number of plantlets by tissue culture method is called:
126409.sol: Micropropagation or tissue culture is the practice of rapidly multiplying stock plant material to produce many progeny plants, using modern plant tissue culture methods. It facilitates the growth, storage, and maintenance of a large number of plants in small spaces which makes it a costeffective process. Micropropagation is used for germplasm storage and the protection of endangered species.

126490.subject: Botany
126490.text: What is the rise per base pair in B-DNA?
126490.sol: There are two hydrogen bonds between A and T in DNA and 3 between G and C. One full turn of the helical strand in DNA involves ten base pairs or ten steps of ascent. Each step of ascent measures 3.4Å. Hence, the pitch of B-DNA is 34Å. The rise per base pair in B-DNA is 3.4Å

126553.subject: Botany
126553.text: Select the correct statement for the figure given below.
options: It gives us a 3-dimensional view of a protein.
The protein thread are folded into other forms like helix and pleated sheets is called the tertiary structure.
In proteins, only right handed helices are observed.
All portions of the protein thread are arranged in the form of a helix.
126553.sol: Of course, only some portions of the protein thread are arranged in the form of a helix. In proteins, only right handed helices are observed. Other regions of the protein thread are folded into other forms in what is called the secondary structure (Fig. 9.3 b). In addition, the long protein chain is also folded upon itself like a hollow woollen ball, giving rise to the tertiary structure (Fig.9.3c). This gives us a 3-dimensional view of a protein.

127461.subject: Botany
127461.text: Which one of the following is related to ex situ conservation of threatened animals and plants?
127461.sol: Ex situ conservation is an offsite strategy for conservation of animals and plants in the zoological park and botanical gardens respectively. Wildlife safari parks are used for the ex situ conservation of threatened animals and plants. They are taken out from their natural habitat and placed in special settings. Here they are protected and given special care.

127623.subject: Botany
127623.text: What is the transfer of energy between organisms at different trophic levels expressed in terms of?
127623.sol: The transfer of energy between organisms at different trophic levels is expressed in terms of number, biomass or energy. This, relationship is expressed in terms of number, biomass or energy. The base of each pyramid represents the producers or the first trophic level while the apex represents tertiary or top level consumer . The three types of ecological pyramids that are usually studied are (a) pyramid of number; (b) pyramid of biomass and (c) pyramid of energy.

128105.subject: Zoology
128105.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Goblet cells of the alimentary canal are classified as unicellular glands. Reason (R): They are formed by the modification of simple squamous epithelial cells to secrete mucus. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
128105.sol: Assertion (A) is true because goblet cells of the alimentary canal consist of isolated glandular cells, which makes them unicellular glands. Reason (R) is false because glandular epithelium is formed by the modification of columnar or cuboidal epithelial cells, not squamous epithelial cells. Squamous epithelium is typically involved in functions like forming diffusion boundaries, whereas columnar and cuboidal cells get specialised for secretion. Therefore, (A) is true but (R) is false. 128905.subject: Zoology
128905.text: What is the cardiac output of an athlete compared to that of an ordinary man?
128905.sol: The cardiac output can be defined as the volume of blood pumped out by each ventricle per minute and averages 5000 mL or 5 litres in a healthy individual. The body has the ability to alter the stroke volume as well as the heart rate and thereby the cardiac output. For example, the cardiac output of an athlete will be much higher than that of an ordinary man.

128990.subject: Zoology
128990.text: Lymphatic Organ Function A. Spleen 1. Maturation of T cells B. Thymus 2. Filters lymph C. Lymph nodes 3. Filters blood D. Tonsils 4. Traps pathogens
128990.sol: The spleen filters blood, removing old or damaged red blood cells and recycling iron. The thymus is the site where T cells mature. Lymph nodes filter lymph, a fluid that contains white blood cells, before it returns to the bloodstream. Tonsils trap pathogens that enter the body through the mouth or nose.

129043.subject: Zoology
129043.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): In a cubic millimeter of healthy human blood, platelets outnumber neutrophils. 129137.subject: Zoology
129137.text: Assertion : The regulation of RBC production is accompanied by the kidneys. Reason : Erythropoietin hormone circulates to the red bone marrow, where it increases stem cell mitosis and speeds up the development of RBCs.
options: If both the assertion and reason are true and reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but assertion is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
If the assertion is true but the reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
129137.sol: The regulation of RBC production is accomplished by the hormone erythropoietin which is secreted by the juxtaglomerular cells of kidney. This hormone circulates to the red bone marrow, where it increases stem cell (myoblasts) mitosis and speeds the development of red blood cells

129636.subject: Zoology
129636.text: Type of Excretion Example A. Ammonotelism 1. Birds B. Ureotelism 2. Mammals C. Uricotelism 3. Aquatic animals D. Guanotelism 4. Spiders and scorpions
129636.sol: Ammonotelism is seen in aquatic animals like fish, where ammonia is excreted. Ureotelism is typical in mammals, where urea is the main excretory product. Uricotelism occurs in birds and reptiles, where uric acid is excreted. Guanotelism is found in some arachnids, such as spiders and scorpions, where guanine is excreted.

129832.subject: Zoology
options: The additional volume of air a person can expire by a forceful expiration
The volume of air a person can inspire during a normal inspiration
The volume of air a person can inspire by a forceful inspiration
The volume of air a person can expire during a normal expiration
129832.sol: Tidal Volume (TV): Volume of air inspired or expired during a normal respiration. It is approx. 500 mL., i.e., a healthy man can inspire or expire approximately 6000 to 8000 mL of air per minute. Inspiratory Reserve Volume (IRV): Additional volume of air, a person can inspire by a forcible inspiration. This averages 2500 mL to 3000 mL. Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV): Additional volume of air, a person can expire by a forcible expiration. This averages 1000 mL to 1100 mL.

It causes irreversible distension and loss of elasticity of alveoli. As a result, the alveolar sacs remain filled with air even after expiration. The exhalation becomes more difficult. 130870.text: What is the function of the mammary ampulla in a mammary gland?

The glandular tissue of each breast is divided into 15-20 mammary lobes containing clusters of cells called alveoli. 131930.text: Assertion : In eukaryotes, both intron and exon are transcribed to form hnRNA. Reason : Splicing is required in prokaryotes.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
131930.sol: Eukaryotic transcripts possess extra segments called introns or intervening sequences or non-coding sequences. They do not appear in mature or processed RNA. The functional coding sequences are called exons. Splicing is removal of introns and fusion of exons to form functional RNAs. Splicing is generally not required in prokaryotes.

They exploited the variations that were naturally present in the wild populations of plants and animals to selectively breed and select for organisms that possessed desirable characters. They replicated his experiments exactly without any changes
They focused on different organisms entirely

133023.subject: Zoology
133023.text: What was the most significant trend in the evolution of modern man (Homo sapiens) from his ancestors?
133023.sol: Modern man (Homo sapiens sapiens) is most evolved. The most significant trend in the evolution of modern man (Homo sapiens) from his ancestors is the gradual increase in the cranial capacity. Cranial capacity of modern man is an average of 1450 cc .
